title: DFA on 80% COC completion: I don't think its a failure
summary: The DFA said reaching 80% completion on the South China Sea Code of Conduct is not a "failure," and that the Philippines has done what it can under its chairmanship of the ASEAN.

blocks.text: The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) on Monday said reaching 80% completion on the South China Sea Code of Conduct (COC) is not a "failure," and that the Philippines has done what it can under its chairmanship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit given the time period.

"We have done 80% or more than that. So I don't think it's a failure. I think we have done what we have to do as far as Philippines as chair," DFA Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro said in a press briefing on Monday.
"But we did have more time. I don't know what's wrong with that," she added.

Lazaro reiterated that the COC failed to reach its completion under the Philippines' chairmanship due to time constraints in the negotiations. She earlier said that the COC will be completed in 2027, during Singapore's turn as ASEAN chair.
"It's just that we lack material time. If we were given another five to six months, we could have finished it," she said.
China and Malaysia currently chair the COC negotiations until mid-2027, then China and Lao will chair it for the remainder of the year.

The proposed code seeks to establish rules to prevent disputes in the South China Sea from escalating and developing into a major armed conflict that could involve the United States, a Philippine ally, and other countries in the region.
The Philippines will pass its ASEAN chairmanship to Singapore.
"To say that it will finish for 2027. Now, we give it to Singapore probably under the way they're shepherding the whole thing," Lazaro said.
"But I don't think I can give you a timeline as to when the Code of Conduct will finish," she added. — BM, GMA News
